1  DHARWAD-580 001.
 ...RESPONDENT

(BY SRI. PRAVEENA Y. DEVAREDDIYAVARA, HCGP)
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED U/SEC. 438 OF CR.P.C.
 (U/SEC. 482 OF BNSS) SEEKING TO GRANT OF ANTICIPATORY BAIL  ON SUCH TERMS AND CONDITIONS AS DEEMED FIT IN THE EVENT  OF HER ARREST IN GADAG CEN CRIME NO. 62/2024 FOR THE  OFFENCES P/U/SC. 418 AND 420 R/W 34 OF IPC. IN SO FAR  ACCUSED NO.2 IS CONCERNED.
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:14869  CRL.P No. 102935 of 2024

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C M JOSHI)
1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent-State.

2. Factual matrix of the case is that petitioner, who is arrayed as accused No.2 in FIR, is wife of accused No.1 and accused Nos. 1 to 6 together represented to 38 persons including complainant that during COVID many of appointments in Government Departments are held up and Government is contemplating to make appointments and they would provide such appointments to these 38 persons; and had collected sum of Rs.3,30,25,000/-; later they did not arrange for employment and therefore, a case came to be filed in Crime No.62/2024 of Gadag CEN police station.
The FIR also mentions that a sum of Rs.70,00,000/- has been repaid and a sum of Rs.2,59,75,000/- is yet to returned by accused.
There is specific allegation that accused Nos.1, 2 to 6 were involved in collecting money by representing that 38 persons including complainant would be provided employment.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that accused No.1 has been granted bail by trail Court and accused No.2, only because she was wife of accused No.1, is arraigned as an accused; and all transactions, which are alleged in FIR are against remaining accused and therefore,
he submits that there is absolutely no material to show role of petitioner/accused No.2 in commission of offence.
4.
Learned HCGP would submit that accused No.2 had assisted accused No.1 and other accused in collecting money and therefore, she is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: 5. On careful perusal of the records, it is seen that there is no specific allegation against accused No.2 in the FIR.
The allegations are mainly against accused Nos.1, 3 to 6, who have allegedly cheated 38 persons promising that employment would be given.
Question that needs to be thrashed out before trial Court is whether accused had intention to usurp money for their unlawful gain knowing that they are unable to provide employment to people.
It would not be proper to say anything on such intention that may emanate from trial.

However, petitioner/accused No.2 being wife of accused No.1, being a NC: 2024:KHC-D:14869 lady is not shown to be actively involved in collecting money and therefore, she would be entitled for anticipatory bail.
Hence, petition deserves to be allowed and following order is passed.
ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.
In the event of arrest of petitioner/accused No.2 in Crime No.62/2024 of Gadag CEN Police Station for offences punishable under Sections 418, 420 R/w Section 34 of IPC, she is ordered to be enlarged on bail subject to following conditions:
i) The petitioner shall furnish personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the trial Court;
ii) The petitioner shall appear before investigating officer within 15 days from the date of this order and co-operate for the investigation, as and when necessary;
NC: 2024:KHC-D:14869 iii) The petitioner shall furnish her residential address and other contact details to investigating officer of CEN Police Station, Gadag within 15 days from the date of this order.
iv) The petitioner shall not tamper with prosecution evidence or witnesses directly or indirectly in whatsoever manner;
It is made clear that any lapse in this regard would entail cancellation of bail.
